name: Route 66
title: Route 66 — One Stop at a Time
description: Route 66 roadside memories from Missouri to the Santa Monica Pier, arranged east to west from separate trips: Devil’s Elbow, Cadillac Ranch, the Blue Hole, Winslow, and more filmed stops.
hero_alt: A scene from the film Route 66, One Stop at a Time.
intro: Route 66 gave them more reasons to stop than to hurry. These films gather roadside memories from Missouri to the Santa Monica Pier: small towns, old bridges, Oklahoma neon, Cadillac Ranch, the Blue Hole, Lowell Observatory — where Pluto was discovered in 1930 — and the people and places they wanted to remember.

The footage comes from separate trips, arranged east to west. It is not one continuous drive, and they have not driven every mile. The map line follows Route 66 roughly between the stops that appear in the films. It is a guide to the road, not a record of a single journey.

stops.name: Totem Pole Trading Post
stops.note: A Route 66 trading post on Martin Springs Drive in Rolla, seen in the Missouri film.

then_and_now.text: The trading post closed in September 2024, and the building was demolished in May 2025.
then_and_now.source_note: Ron Warnick, “Totem Pole Trading Post in Rolla, one of Twin Bridges near Catoosa torn down,” Route 66 News, May 14, 2025: Josh Thompson photographed the demolition on May 7, 2025; the post closed in late September 2024. Closure on Sept. 30, 2024 also reported by Allison Skinner, Phelps County Focus, Sept. 23, 2024, https://phelpscountyfocus.com/2024/09/23/open-since-1933-totem-pole-trading-post-doors-closing-sept-30/.
